value.title: Introduction to Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP)
value.summary: The video begins by introducing the MLP structure, illustrating its components through a diagram with arrows representing data flow. It explains the initial linear transformation of input vectors and highlights the limitation of purely linear operations in modeling non-linear phenomena like language. The concept of passing intermediate vectors through a non-linear function is introduced as a solution.

value.title: Non-Linear Transformations with ReLU and GELU
value.summary: The video demonstrates how linear inputs are transformed using non-linear activation functions, specifically ReLU and GELU. It explains the ReLU function's behavior—clipping negative values to zero while preserving positive ones—and its role in mimicking an AND gate. The visual and dialogue content together clarify how these functions enable neural networks to model complex, non-linear relationships.

value.title: Parameter Counting and Architecture of GPT-3
value.summary: The video details the parameter distribution in GPT-3, focusing on the MLP blocks and their contribution to the total 175 billion parameters. It breaks down the up-projection and down-projection matrices, bias terms, and their roles in the model’s computation. The explanation emphasizes that MLPs account for about two-thirds of the total parameters in the network.

value.title: Superposition and High-Dimensional Vector Spaces
value.summary: The video explores the concept of superposition in high-dimensional spaces, explaining how features can be represented by nearly orthogonal vectors. It uses the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma to illustrate that in high dimensions, many vectors can be nearly perpendicular, enabling efficient representation. This concept helps explain why large language models are both powerful and difficult to interpret.

value.title: Locality Sensitive Hashing and Conclusion
value.summary: The video concludes by introducing the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and its connection to Locality Sensitive Hashing, reinforcing the idea that high-dimensional spaces allow for efficient, scalable representations. The final moments tie together the technical concepts, emphasizing the mathematical foundation behind modern transformer architectures.
